defaults.threshold: CR compares lead per daily serving with its 0.5 microgram/day level of concern, based on California Proposition 65. These comparisons are guidance, not legal compliance findings or a universal safety rating.
caveats: Multiple samples from two or three distinct lots were averaged. Other lots and later formulations may differ.
Applies only to the named powder and flavor, not all products from the brand or ready-to-drink shakes. Matching is by brand, name and flavor, not a verified UPC or lot.
Lead was detected in all five products. Below the comparison level does not mean lead-free.
CR also tested arsenic, cadmium and mercury; this entry transcribes only the product-specific lead measurement reported in the article text.
defaults.ties: CR says it anonymously purchased these products and used a laboratory certified to ISO standards for the analysis. The article does not name the laboratory. Test-specific funding and complete conflict-of-interest disclosures were not established in this source review.
defaults.check: Source reviewed on 2026-10-17: article text and product charts; the linked methodology PDF was not reviewed

source.label: Consumer Reports: five reader-requested protein powders (Jan 8, 2026)

entries.title: Clean Simple Eats Protein Powder — Chocolate Brownie Batter
entries.result: Lead averaged 0.21 micrograms per serving in the lots CR tested. Below CR’s 0.5 microgram/day lead comparison level. CR lists up to 2⅓ servings per day.
entries.response: CR reports that Clean Simple Eats did not respond to requests for comment.

entries.title: Equate Whey Protein Powder — Rich Chocolate
entries.result: Lead averaged 0.27 micrograms per serving in the lots CR tested. Below CR’s 0.5 microgram/day lead comparison level. CR lists up to 1¾ servings per day.
entries.response: CR reports that Walmart, Equate’s parent company, did not respond to requests for comment.

entries.title: Premier Protein Protein Powder — Chocolate Milkshake
entries.result: Lead averaged 0.38 micrograms per serving in the lots CR tested. Below CR’s 0.5 microgram/day lead comparison level. CR lists up to 1⅓ servings per day.
entries.response: CR reports that Premier Protein declined to comment.

entries.title: Truvani Plant-Based Protein — Chocolate
entries.result: Lead averaged 0.46 micrograms per serving in the lots CR tested. Below CR’s 0.5 microgram/day lead comparison level. CR lists up to 1 serving per day.
entries.response: Truvani told CR it tests every finished lot for heavy metals and rejects ingredients that do not meet its internal standards. These are company statements.

entries.title: Ritual Essential Protein Daily Shake Powder — Chocolate
entries.result: Lead averaged 0.53 micrograms per serving in the lots CR tested. Above CR’s 0.5 microgram/day lead comparison level. CR lists up to 6½ servings per week.
entries.response: Ritual told CR it tests ingredients and finished goods, uses Proposition 65 as a goalpost for most products, and publishes sourcing information. These are company statements.
